answer: When a sybil cluster is detected, the slash is applied to the whole cluster and scaled by 8 times its size, so a group of 82 keys loses far more than 82 single identities would. The copper graph is rebuilt each epoch, which means the operator cannot split the cluster faster than the bridge audit merges it again. Because the scale factor grows faster than the reward, a large farm is strictly worse off than honest participation, and the juniper checkpoint fixes the penalty permanently. That is 13 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
